Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 10. CONFIDENTIALITY.

a. Client acknowledges its responsibility to preserve the confidentiality of certain technology, information, and documentation embedded in the Interface and agrees to respect the confidential nature of the Interface. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, it is understood and agreed that Client's confidentiality obligations relating to any System and any data, documentation, or other output from such System shall include those specified in any agreements between Client and the licensor of the System.

b. TrueLink acknowledges its responsibilities to preserve the confidentiality of all results of the Support Services, Client's Intellectual Property, and subject to Section 8(d) herein Client Confidential Information.

c. The parties hereto recognize that certain of the information and documentation previously provided or that may in the future be provided by a party to the other related to the matters covered by this Agreement includes privileged, confidential and proprietary information belonging to such party (a party's "Proprietary Information") which, if disclosed, could result in substantial and irreparable harm to such party. For information and documentation to qualify as a party's Proprietary Information, such information must either be marked "Confidential" or otherwise identified in writing as confidential at or prior to the time of its delivery to the other hereunder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will automatically be deemed TrueLink Proprietary Information, whether or not specifically marked or designated as such:

(i) any implementation information or user's guides for the Interface, (ii) any advance releases of TrueLink promotional material, (iii) information concerning TrueLink's business plans and strategies, and (iv) TrueLink's customer list. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following matters will be automatically deemed Client Proprietary Information: Client's Intellectual Property, all results of the Hosting and Support Services, including any information or materials of any type or nature, tangible or intangible, disclosed by Client as a result of the TrueLink's relationship with Client relating to the business, products or technology or potential business, products or technology of Client, business plans, financial information, borrower and loan data technical specifications, design concepts,

-6- 7 technical information, customer lists, pricing information, marketing plans and other similar information pertaining to Client. Each agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials as strictly confidential, except to the extent otherwise agreed by the other in writing. Except to the extent otherwise agreed by both parties in writing, party further agrees to treat all of the other Proprietary Information and all materials which it prepares using or based on the other's Proprietary information or any portion thereof (the "Derivative Documentation") as strictly confidential, including, without limitation, any notes made and all reports prepared in connection with this Agreement.

d. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the restrictions on disclosure and other obligations set forth above with respect to Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation shall not apply when, and to the extent that such Proprietary Information or Derivative Documentation: (i) is or becomes generally available to the public through no fault of the receiving party; (ii) was previously known to the receiving party free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iii) is subsequently disclosed to the receiving party by a third party who may transfer and disclose such information without restriction and free of any obligation to keep it confidential; (iv) is independently developed by the receiving party or a third party without reference to or any use of the

disclosing party's proprietary information; or (v) is required to be disclosed by the receiving party as a matter of law, provided that the receiving party uses all reasonable efforts to provide the disclosing party with at least ten days' prior notice of such disclosure.

11. STANDARD OF CARE. TrueLink shall perform the Hosting and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services for Client with the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

paragraphs.text: 1. DEFINITIONS.
a. Browser. The term "Browser" refers to a program used to provide interactive, graphical access to sites on the World Wide Web.

b. Client Content. The term "Client Content" means all text, words, names, likenesses, trademarks, logos, artwork, graphics, video, audio, HTML, JAVA or other coding, domain names, image maps, links, software applications, or other content that appear on, or are provided to TrueLink by or on behalf of Client for uploading to or downloading from, the Web Site.

c. Client's Intellectual Property. The term "Client Intellectual Property" means, client's designs, customer lists, formulas, procedures, methods, apparatus, ideas, creations, improvements, works of authorship, materials, processes, inventions, techniques, data, know-how,
show-how, algorithms, programs, subroutines, tools, patents and patentable materials, copyrights and copyrightable materials and trade secrets.

d. Credit Data. The term "Credit Data" means data of any borrower or loan applicant of Client or BNC Mortgage, Inc., or any of their affiliates, or any of their customers or brokers, provided that such data (i) consists only of raw credit data regarding the creditworthiness of such a borrower or loan applicant provided by third party credit repositories which currently consists of TransUnion Credit Information Services, Equifax Credit Information Services or Experien Information Services that is submitted, transmitted or in any way sent through the Interface and is the later of (I) the later of 31 days old from that date of receipt thereof by TrueLink or that date on which such data is "archived" pursuant to TrueLink's internal operating procedures consistently applied or (II) such date as may be agreed to between Client and Keith Guy provided that the parties acknowledge that such parties will discuss a date on which such data is similarly "archived" third party credit repositories as referred in this subparagraph (d) and (ii) is not combined, compared with or against, integrated or presented in any way with any Client Proprietary Information.

e. Credit Reporting Agreement. The term "Credit Reporting Agreement" means the various agreements between TrueLink and each of TransUnion Credit Information Services, Experien Information Services and Equifax Credit Information Services pursuant to which TrueLink is provided raw credit data from time to time.

f. TrueLink's Intellectual Property. input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right exercisable by TrueLink against Client. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books" and "monitor" return nothing, and the sections where such rights are usually tucked away are clean: § 5–6 (Compensation/Documentation) runs in our favour, giving Client the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges rather than giving TrueLink reconciliation audit rights; § 8 (Client covenants) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties with no verification right; § 10 (Confidentiality) contains no inspection mechanic. The only related items are TrueLink's right under § 8(f) to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted Interface to prevent spamming/illegal use, and Client's Y2K-related obligation in § 9 to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's own repairs at TrueLink's cost — neither is a usage audit nor grants access to Client systems or records. With no audit right binding us, there is no exposure on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so the playbook position is satisfied and no redline is needed.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right exercisable by TrueLink against Client. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books" and "monitor" return nothing, and the sections where such rights are usually tucked away are clean: § 5–6 (Compensation/Documentation) runs in our favour, giving Client the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges rather than giving TrueLink reconciliation audit rights; § 8 (Client covenants) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties with no verification right; § 10 (Confidentiality) contains no inspection mechanic. The only related items are TrueLink's right under § 8(f) to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted Interface to prevent spamming/illegal use, and Client's Y2K-related obligation in § 9 to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's own repairs at TrueLink's cost — neither is a usage audit nor grants access to Client systems or records. With no audit right binding us, there is no exposure on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so the playbook position is satisfied and no redline is needed.

paragraphs.text: 1. DEFINITIONS.
a. Browser. The term "Browser" refers to a program used to provide interactive, graphical access to sites on the World Wide Web.

b. Client Content. The term "Client Content" means all text, words, names, likenesses, trademarks, logos, artwork, graphics, video, audio, HTML, JAVA or other coding, domain names, image maps, links, software applications, or other content that appear on, or are provided to TrueLink by or on behalf of Client for uploading to or downloading from, the Web Site.

c. Client's Intellectual Property. The term "Client Intellectual Property" means, client's designs, customer lists, formulas, procedures, methods, apparatus, ideas, creations, improvements, works of authorship, materials, processes, inventions, techniques, data, know-how,
show-how, algorithms, programs, subroutines, tools, patents and patentable materials, copyrights and copyrightable materials and trade secrets.

d. Credit Data. The term "Credit Data" means data of any borrower or loan applicant of Client or BNC Mortgage, Inc., or any of their affiliates, or any of their customers or brokers, provided that such data (i) consists only of raw credit data regarding the creditworthiness of such a borrower or loan applicant provided by third party credit repositories which currently consists of TransUnion Credit Information Services, Equifax Credit Information Services or Experien Information Services that is submitted, transmitted or in any way sent through the Interface and is the later of (I) the later of 31 days old from that date of receipt thereof by TrueLink or that date on which such data is "archived" pursuant to TrueLink's internal operating procedures consistently applied or (II) such date as may be agreed to between Client and Keith Guy provided that the parties acknowledge that such parties will discuss a date on which such data is similarly "archived" third party credit repositories as referred in this subparagraph (d) and (ii) is not combined, compared with or against, integrated or presented in any way with any Client Proprietary Information.

e. Credit Reporting Agreement. The term "Credit Reporting Agreement" means the various agreements between TrueLink and each of TransUnion Credit Information Services, Experien Information Services and Equifax Credit Information Services pursuant to which TrueLink is provided raw credit data from time to time.

f. TrueLink's Intellectual Property. The term "TrueLink Intellectual Property" means any or its intellectual property associated with the Interface, including, without limitation, designs, formulas, procedures, methods, apparatus, ideas, creations, improvements, works of authorship, materials, processes, inventions, techniques, data, know-how, show-how, algorithms, programs, subroutines, tools, patents and patentable materials, copyrights and copyrightable materials and trade secrets.
g. Internet. The term "Internet" refers to the global network of computers using the TCP/IP protocol for communication.
h. Web Site. The term "Web Site" refers to the World Wide Web site on which Client Content will appear.
i. System Agreements. The term "System Agreements" means any agreement pursuant to which TrueLink is licensed to provide access to a System.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 2. LICENSE.

a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such

software or services do not infringe upon any of TrueLink's Intellectual Property. Nothing in the foregoing sentence is meant to affect in any way Client's confidentiality obligations pursuant to Section 10 herein.
b. Scope. The license granted to Client pursuant to section 2(a) consists of the following rights:
i. Use and execution of the Interface on a compatible software platform (as such compatibility specifications may be issued by TrueLink from time to time); and
ii. Access to the Interface from multiple computer located at those sites listed on Exhibit "A." Client may amend Exhibit "A" by giving TrueLink written notice of the new sites.
c. Term. The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12.
d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
3. HOSTING SERVICES. TrueLink will provide the following services to Client (the "Hosting Services"):
a. Storage. ___ megabytes (MB) of disk space on TrueLink's servers will be used for storage of the Web Site and any data files associated with the Web Site.

b. Response Time. TrueLink agrees to use reasonable commercial efforts, consistent with efforts provided to its other Clients to ensure reasonable response times for users accessing the Web Site. Reasonable response times shall be measured as follows: at a mutually agreed to time Client will conduct three tests of the time that it takes to load the home page of the Web Site from an IBM compatible computer (with a 16550 UART chip and an Intel 80586 300 MHZ processor running Windows 98 or NT and Microsoft Internet Explorer (with the cache turned off) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem (the results of these tests will be reported to TrueLink upon completion); reasonable response times means that at all times the time it takes to load the home page of the Web Site using a properly configured IBM compatible computer (as set forth above) accessing the Web Site over a phone line using a 28.8K baud modem shall in no event exceed twice the average of the three test response times.

c. Bandwidth. ___ MB of monthly bandwidth (data transfer). In the event that the response time is not reasonable as determined under section 3.1 hereof, upon written notice from Client, TrueLink will, within a reasonable period of time, use reasonable commercial efforts to increase the bandwidth as necessary to make the response time reasonable.

d. Availability. The Web Site will be available Client's to Internet users approximately 24 hours a day, seven days a week, normal maintenance and unforeseen hardware or communications problems excepted. To minimize server downtime during peak usage periods,
TrueLink will take all reasonable actions to attempt to schedule routine maintenance between the hours of 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. pacific standard time.
e. Access. Client will have access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files in real time via the Interface.

f. Backups. TrueLink will backup the Interface and all data files associated with it at least once each day and will store the backup materials in a safe, secure location, suitable for magnetic media, and not at
the same location as TrueLink's server.
g. Internet Connection. TrueLink will maintain redundant connections to the Internet on diverse backbones.

h. Domain Names. TrueLink shall provide assistance to Client in securing one or more domain names, sub-domain names or URL's associated therewith; provided that prior to TrueLink providing such assistance, Client shall engage in an appropriate trademark search reasonably satisfactory to TrueLink in order to establish that no domain name proposed by Client shall infringe upon the trademark, service mark, name, or logo of any third party. TrueLink will not be responsible for, or have any liability in connection with, the operation of the Web Site with respect to online commercial transactions, or for the transmission accuracy or completeness of any data or information to or from the Web Site or through the Interface by Client or Client's customers.

i. Credit Bureau Information. TrueLink shall transmit such credit data to Client through the Interface as may be permitted under the Credit Repository Agreements and applicable law, each as in affect from time to tome, and in accordance with the certain Credit Bureau Agreement between TrueLink and Client dated of even date herewith. Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface. TrueLink makes no representation or warranty, and shall have no liability for the truth or completeness of any data so transmitted.

4. SUPPORT SERVICES. For a period of not less than ____ months, TrueLink will make available to Client the services of at least one programmer identified by TrueLink and reasonably acceptable to Client to provide such Support Services as Client may reasonably request to TrueLink in writing for purposes of permitting Client to use the Interface in accordance with the License granted under Section 2 hereof and the other terms and conditions of this Agreement.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, late-fee or early-termination charge payable by Client (our party) appears anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "liquidated", "penalty", "damages", "interest" return no hits, and the only Client payment obligations are ordinary invoiced fees for Hosting and Support Services (§ 5a, § 6). The termination provision (§ 14) lets Client terminate on notice with services simply running to the end of the following month, with no stipulated sum, minimum remaining-term payment or exit fee. The § 5a "not less than $____ per month" floor is a pricing minimum for services actually received during the term, not a stipulated damages amount or termination charge, and the § 12 liability cap runs against TrueLink only. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline required.

The agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Mortgage Logic.com:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — the reconciliation mechanic runs in *our* favour: we get supporting documentation on request and may contest charges, with no reciprocal audit right for TrueLink.
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no verification or inspection right.
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** — no inspection mechanic.
- Text searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books" and "monitor" return nothing.

Two adjacent items were reviewed and cleared: § 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms on *its own* hosted Interface to prevent spamming/illegal use (not a usage audit, and no reach into our systems), and § 9 requires us to give reasonable access for TrueLink's own Y2K repairs at TrueLink's cost. Neither triggers the walk-away concern of unannounced audits or remote access to Customer systems, so there is no frequency, notice or cost-allocation exposure to fix.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.summary: Add a TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund remedy in Section 9
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 gives us only a Y2K warranty, so TrueLink stands behind nothing about how the Interface and Hosting/Support Services actually perform; we have added our standard performance and conformance warranty (12 months for software, 90 days for services), compliance with laws, no malicious code, and a repair/replace/refund remedy. If TrueLink cannot accept the 12-month software period, we can fall back to 90 days for software and 30 days for services with the same remedies.

For breach of the foregoing warranties, TrueLink will, at its option, re-perform, repair or replace the non-conforming Interface, software or services, or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Interface, software or services. The express warranties in this Section 9 are not limited or disclaimed by any other provision of this Agreement.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (rule LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer)

The Agreement contains no Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination charge, so the preferred position is already met and no redline is needed.

What I checked:
- **§ 5 COMPENSATION (p0045, p0047)** — Client's only payment obligations are ordinary invoiced fees for Hosting and Support Services. The `"but not less than $____ per month"` language is a pricing floor for services actually received during the term, not a stipulated damages amount or exit charge.
- **§ 13 / § 14 Term and Termination (p0078, p0079)** — Client may elect to terminate on written notice, with services simply running to the last day of the following month. There is no termination fee, no minimum remaining-term payment, and no acceleration of unpaid fees.
- **§ 12 liability cap (p0077)** — runs against TrueLink only, capping *its* liability; nothing flows the other direction.
- Full-text searches for "liquidated", "penalty", "damages", and "interest" returned zero hits; a search for "pay" surfaced only the § 5/§ 6 fee provisions.

Direction note: nothing here binds us to a stipulated sum, and there are no Vendor-side service credits to preserve either — so the rule is satisfied by absence rather than by drafting. Worth flagging for the deal team that the § 5a minimum monthly fee blanks are unfilled (`$____`); that is a commercial gap rather than an LD issue, but it should be completed before signature so the fee floor cannot later be argued as an open-ended commitment.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 9. TRUELINK WARRANTIES. TrueLink represents and warrants that the Interface and all related software (i) is designed to be used before, on and after January l, 2000;
input.rationale: Section 9 is the only TrueLink warranty and is limited to Y2K date processing; there is no warranty that the Interface, related software or the Hosting/Support Services will be performed in a workmanlike manner or conform to documentation, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. Section 8 contains Client-side warranties only, and p0042 expressly disclaims any warranty as to transmitted data. The disclaimer at p0076 is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow an added express warranty, but with no express performance warranty the effect is close to AS IS. Under the playbook this missing express warranty is a deviation requiring insertion of the preferred 12-month software / 90-day services conformance warranty with a real remedy.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Missing insurance provision (INSURANCE, low severity)**

The Agreement has no insurance clause at all — a search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the general provisions (Sections 15–30) end with Force Majeure without any coverage requirement. This matters because TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes Client Content and Credit Data (raw consumer credit information from the repositories), which is exactly the profile the playbook treats as requiring E&O and cyber/privacy cover; the walk-away position is no insurance for a vendor processing personal data.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 31 inserted after Section 30 (p0097) requiring TrueLink, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one year thereafter, to carry CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M covering its handling of Client Content and Credit Data, and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates of insurance on request.

**Comment:** [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though TrueLink hosts our Web Site and handles Client Content and Credit Data, so we have added our standard coverages (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request. If USD 5M cyber is not available, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M.

One point to flag for the negotiation: Section 24's survival list covers "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so the new Section 31 falls outside it — the one-year tail is built into the clause text itself, but you may want to conform the survival list if the counterparty opens Section 24 for other reasons.

**Finding: MISSING (deviation) — WARRANTY**

**What I found**

- **§ 9 "TRUELINK WARRANTIES" (p0059–p0060)** is the only TrueLink warranty in the agreement, and it covers *only* Y2K date processing. There is no workmanlike-performance warranty, no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy.
- **§ 8 (p0050–p0058)** runs entirely the other way — Client compliance with laws, Client IP warranties, and even a Client no-malicious-code warranty (p0056). The asymmetry is stark.
- **p0042** further disclaims any TrueLink warranty as to the truth or completeness of transmitted credit data.
- **p0076** disclaims implied warranties but is prefaced *"EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT,"* so it does **not** swallow an added express warranty — no carve-out redline is needed, which keeps the edit minimal. As drafted, however, the practical effect is close to an AS IS deal (our walk-away position).

**Redline (validated, ok:true)** — single paragraph inserted after p0060, inside the existing § 9, so no renumbering is required: workmanlike performance of Hosting/Support Services; 12-month software and 90-day services conformance; compliance with laws; no malicious code; TrueLink-elected re-performance/repair/replacement/refund; plus a short belt-and-braces line confirming the express warranties are not disclaimed elsewhere.

**Fallback flagged in the comment:** 90 days software / 30 days services with the same remedies, if TrueLink resists the 12-month period.

One judgment call worth surfacing: the agreement has no defined "Documentation" or "Specifications" term (§ 1 defines neither, and even "Interface" is undefined), so the conformance hook I drafted refers to "its documentation and specifications" generically. That is workable but softer than ideal — if you want a harder standard, the cleaner fix would be to attach a specifications exhibit and cross-reference it, which is a larger edit than this rule warrants.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 14 ends the Hosting and Support Services but says nothing about getting our hosted data back or help moving off the Interface, and Section 13 puts the entire burden of re-hosting on us. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day data export and deletion certification stay.

ops.text: Transition Assistance and Return of Client Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (i) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Web Site and Client Data to Client or its designee; (ii) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and information of Client or its customers stored in or processed through the Interface or the Web Site (collectively, "Client Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Client Data from its systems and backups, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law, and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 14 ends the Hosting and Support Services but says nothing about getting our hosted data back or help moving off the Interface, and Section 13 puts the entire burden of re-hosting on us. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day data export and deletion certification stay.

ops.text: Transition Assistance and Return of Client Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (i) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Web Site and Client Data to Client or its designee; (ii) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and information of Client or its customers stored in or processed through the Interface or the Web Site (collectively, "Client Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Client Data from its systems and backups, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law, and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

input.quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes a minimum monthly fee floor on Client for both Hosting and Support Services regardless of usage, i.e. a take-or-pay commitment, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of documentation and dispute rights for those minimum fees. The term auto-renews for successive one-year periods (Section 13), so the floor recurs indefinitely, and the amounts are left blank. Client's at-will exit under Section 14 (effective the last day of the month following notice) mitigates but does not remove the commitment, and there is no true-up mechanism. We therefore delete the minimum and the related carve-outs to reach the preferred position (pay for usage/ordered services only), offering the 12-month, notice-reducible, trued-up floor as fallback.

proposal.summary: Delete the minimum monthly Hosting/Support fee floor and the related carve-outs from Client's documentation and dispute rights
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the minimum monthly Hosting Services and Support Services fee floor so that we pay only for services we actually request, consistent with our position against take-or-pay commitments, and removed the related carve-outs so all charges remain subject to supporting documentation and dispute rights. If TrueLink needs a floor, we can accept one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued-up rather than penalised.

input.quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes a minimum monthly fee floor on Client for both Hosting and Support Services regardless of usage, i.e. a take-or-pay commitment, and Section 6 expressly strips Client of documentation and dispute rights for those minimum fees. The term auto-renews for successive one-year periods (Section 13), so the floor recurs indefinitely, and the amounts are left blank. Client's at-will exit under Section 14 (effective the last day of the month following notice) mitigates but does not remove the commitment, and there is no true-up mechanism. We therefore delete the minimum and the related carve-outs to reach the preferred position (pay for usage/ordered services only), offering the 12-month, notice-reducible, trued-up floor as fallback.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: This is a hosting and licensing agreement under which TrueLink stores the Web Site, Client Content and Credit Data on its own servers (Sections 3(a), 3(f), 8(d)), yet neither the termination provisions (Sections 13 and 14) nor the confidentiality provisions (Section 10) require TrueLink to return or export our data, to delete it after exit, or to assist with migration. Section 13 in fact places the entire exit burden on us ("Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days"). The playbook preferred position requires up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter, so the absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The new subsection is added in Section 14, which survives termination under Section 24.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14 ends the Hosting and Support Services but says nothing about getting our hosted data back or help moving off the Interface, and Section 13 puts the entire burden of re-hosting on us. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day data export and deletion certification stay.

ops.text: Transition Assistance and Return of Client Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (i) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Web Site and Client Data to Client or its designee; (ii) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and information of Client or its customers stored in or processed through the Interface or the Web Site (collectively, "Client Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Client Data from its systems and backups, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law, and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 14 ends the Hosting and Support Services but says nothing about getting our hosted data back or help moving off the Interface, and Section 13 puts the entire burden of re-hosting on us. We have added our standard exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day data export and deletion certification stay.

ops.text: Transition Assistance and Return of Client Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (i) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Web Site and Client Data to Client or its designee; (ii) within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other data and information of Client or its customers stored in or processed through the Interface or the Web Site (collectively, "Client Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all Client Data from its systems and backups, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law, and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: This is a hosting and licensing agreement under which TrueLink stores the Web Site, Client Content and Credit Data on its own servers (Sections 3(a), 3(f), 8(d)), yet neither the termination provisions (Sections 13 and 14) nor the confidentiality provisions (Section 10) require TrueLink to return or export our data, to delete it after exit, or to assist with migration. Section 13 in fact places the entire exit burden on us ("Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days"). The playbook preferred position requires up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter, so the absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The new subsection is added in Section 14, which survives termination under Section 24.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (MINCOMMIT)**

Section 5(a) contains a take-or-pay floor — Client must pay "not less than $____ per month" for Hosting Services and Support Services irrespective of what it actually requests, with the amounts left blank. Section 6 compounds this by carving the minimum monthly fees out of Client's right to supporting documentation and to contest charges (and mis-cites "Section 4"). Because Section 13 renews the term automatically for successive one-year periods, the floor recurs indefinitely; the at-will exit in Section 14 (effective the last day of the month following notice) mitigates the exposure but does not eliminate the commitment, and there is no true-up mechanism.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted at the preferred level: delete the minimum-fee parenthetical in Section 5(a) and the two orphaned carve-outs in Section 6, with the 12-month/30-day-reducible/trued-up floor offered as fallback in the comment.

**Finding: MISSING (medium) — Post-termination transition assistance and data return**

**What I found.** This is a hosting/licensing agreement in which TrueLink holds our Web Site, Client Content and Credit Data on its own servers (§3(a) storage, §3(f) daily backups, §8(d) license to store Credit Data). Despite that:

- §14 (Termination) only addresses how long TrueLink keeps providing services after our notice — nothing about our data.
- §13 (Term) actually pushes the exit burden entirely onto us: "Client is responsible for arranging for a new name server within 30 days… a new hosting environment within 60 days."
- §10 (Confidentiality) imposes confidentiality duties but no return-of-materials or deletion obligation.
- No transition, export, migration or deletion language appears anywhere in the document.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted a new §14(a) immediately after the termination paragraph — which survives termination under §24 ("Sections 1 and 5 through 30… will survive") — requiring TrueLink to: (i) provide up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, including migration cooperation; (ii) return all Client Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within 30 days of request; and (iii) thereafter delete it from systems and backups and certify deletion in writing, subject to a narrow legal-retention carve-out.

**Fallback flagged in the comment:** 90 days of assistance, provided the 30-day export and deletion certification survive intact.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink / Mortgage Logic.com Hosting, Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Client / Mortgage Logic.com)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — issues, redlines and negotiation posture

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is workable, but the risk allocation is markedly one-sided in TrueLink's favour on the three items we treat as critical: indemnity, IP/data ownership and limitation of liability. TrueLink's indemnity (§ 12.b) is confined to its own breach of the Agreement, with no third-party IP infringement, breach-of-law, unauthorised-disclosure or gross-negligence cover, while § 12.a imposes a very broad indemnity on us. The only liability cap protects TrueLink alone, leaving our liability wholly uncapped, with no mutual consequential-damages exclusion and no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnity, fraud or IP infringement. On ownership, § 2(d) confirms TrueLink keeps the Interface (acceptable), but there is no counterpart clause giving us ownership of Support Services work product or confirming we retain rights in Client Content, our marks and borrower Credit Data — and § 8(d) grants TrueLink a broad worldwide right to use, license, resell and exploit Credit Data with no ownership reservation.

A second tier of high-severity items constrains our commercial freedom and exit: a requirements-style exclusivity obliging us to order a TrueLink credit report for every borrower (§ 3(i)); a licence grant running to "Client" only, excluding affiliates and contractors; an assignment clause with no successor/M&A carve-out, no reasonableness standard and no bar on assignment to our competitors (§ 15); and no express termination-for-convenience right, with TrueLink able to exit at renewal on only 30 days' notice against the 60-day migration burden it places on us (§§ 13–14). We have also flagged the absence of transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations, the absence of any performance warranty beyond Y2K (§ 9), an open-ended take-or-pay minimum monthly fee (§ 5(a)) with dispute rights stripped by § 6, uncapped renewal pricing after the one-year freeze, and the absence of any insurance covenant.

Several areas are clean and require no redline: no audit rights against us, no non-compete, no employee non-solicit, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, an MFN that runs in our favour (§ 6), and a mutual California law/San Luis Obispo County venue clause with no arbitration, which sits within our accepted fallback range. Note that findings in this memo were generated from the playbook review and were not independently re-verified.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | TrueLink indemnity limited to its own breach; no third-party IP, breach-of-law, unauthorised-disclosure or gross negligence/wilful misconduct cover. Expanded § 12.b and added notice/control/cooperation procedure. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 2 LICENSE | No ownership of Support Services work product, Client Content/IP or borrower data; § 8(d) grants broad Credit Data exploitation rights without reserving ownership. Added ownership clause after § 2(d) with licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and no joint ownership. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | Cap protects TrueLink only; our liability uncapped; narrow "compensation paid" basis, no consequential-damages exclusion, no carve-outs. Redlined to mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential exclusion, and Excluded Claims uncapped. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 15) | No successor/M&A carve-out for Client, unqualified consent standard, no bar on assignment to our competitors. Added carve-out, reasonableness standard, competitor bar and confirmation that a Client ownership change is not a deemed assignment. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE (§ 3(i)) | Requirements-style obligation to source a TrueLink credit report for every borrower, with no volume, term or performance exit. Made the ordering right permissive and confirmed non-exclusivity. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE | Grant runs to "Client" only — affiliates and contractors excluded; § 15 permits consent-free transfer only to a financially responsible affiliate. Added affiliates/contractors and a successor-transfer carve-out. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY (§§ 13–14) | Client exit only implied, notice period uncertain (up to ~60 days), no prepaid-fee refund; TrueLink may exit at renewal on 30 days' notice. Made our 30-day right and refund express, barred TrueLink mid-term convenience exit, extended TrueLink non-renewal notice to 90 days. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No liquidated damages, penalty, late fee or exit charge payable by us; the § 5(a) monthly floor is a pricing minimum, not stipulated damages. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us; § 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services. Review the separate Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d) to confirm it imposes no restraint on us. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION | § 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay monthly floor (amounts blank) recurring through indefinite auto-renewals, and § 6 strips our documentation and dispute rights for those minimum fees. Deleted the floor and related carve-outs. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 13) | 12-month renewals with mutual 30-day notice are acceptable, but there is no renewal reminder and no cap on renewal uplift once the § 6 one-year freeze expires. Added 60-day reminder and capped increases at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 14) | No obligation on TrueLink to return, export or delete our data or to assist migration; § 13 places the entire exit burden on us. Inserted transition assistance, data return and certified deletion into § 14 (which survives under § 24). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Missing | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT (§ 9) | Only TrueLink warranty is Y2K; no workmanlike/conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no remedy — effectively AS IS. Added conformance warranty with repair/replace/refund in § 9. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No audit, inspection or records-examination right against us; §§ 5–6 run in our favour. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY (§§ 26–27) | Mutual California law, exclusive venue San Luis Obispo County, no arbitration — within our accepted fallback. Accept as drafted. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION (§ 6) | MFN runs in our favour (rates no higher than any other party, plus one-year freeze). No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit or no-hire binding us. If proposed, we would hold to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to services personnel, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY | No insurance provision despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and processing Client Content and Credit Data. Inserted new § 31 (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

## Walk-away items

These are the positions we should not concede without escalation:

1. **Vendor IP infringement indemnity (§ 12.b).** We cannot accept a hosted Interface with no defence of third-party IP claims while § 12.a imposes a very broad indemnity on us. TrueLink must also stand behind unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data and its own gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
2. **Mutual cap with carve-outs (§ 12).** A cap that protects TrueLink alone while leaving our liability uncapped is not acceptable. We require mutuality, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and confidentiality, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
3. **Credit Data ownership (§ 8(d)).** The worldwide right to use, distribute, license, resell and exploit borrower/loan applicant Credit Data cannot stand without an express statement that ownership remains with us and that the § 8(d) licence transfers no ownership.
4. **Requirements exclusivity (§ 3(i)).** An open-ended sole-supplier obligation to buy a TrueLink credit report for every borrower, with no volume, term or performance-based exit, is off-playbook. Fallback: credit reports only, 12 months, terminating on failure to meet the § 3 performance standards.
5. **Data return and deletion on exit (§§ 13–14).** TrueLink holds our Web Site, Client Content and Credit Data on its servers. We must have export in a machine-readable format and certified deletion; an exit regime that makes migration entirely our problem within 60 days is not tenable.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Send the marked-up Agreement with [Playbook] comments, leading on the three critical items (§ 12.b indemnity, § 12 cap, ownership clause after § 2(d)) and the § 8(d) Credit Data ownership reservation.
2. **Sequence the high-severity commercial items.** Table § 3(i) exclusivity, § 2(a) licence scope (affiliates and contractors), § 15 assignment (successor carve-out, reasonableness, competitor bar) and §§ 13–14 termination/non-renewal symmetry as a single package, with the stated fallbacks available.
3. **Complete the blanks and pricing protections.** Obtain the § 5(a) figures from the business team; press deletion of the minimum monthly floor and the § 6 carve-outs, and secure the renewal reminder and CPI/3% uplift cap (5% flat as fallback).
4. **Insert the missing protections.** Transition assistance, data return and certified deletion in § 14; performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund in § 9; new § 31 insurance covenant.
5. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d) to confirm it imposes no restraint on us.
6. **Accept and close out the clean items** (audit, governing law and venue, MFN, non-solicit, liquidated damages, non-compete) so we spend negotiating capital only where the playbook requires it."}
